title: Introduce SLO Sheath and transient circuit attenuator to reduce rapid flips during regional bursts
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Hotfix: add SLO sheath admission controller and transient circuit attenuator to reduce rapid circuit flips and transient SLO violations during cross-region traffic surges. No API changes.
description: Context: During an incident on 2026-01-29 we observed repeated SLO alert bursts when a regional egress mesh experienced a coordinated traffic spike. The existing circuit breaker recovered correctly, but rapid open/close cycles caused downstream instability and increased tail latency. This PR implements two complementary mitigations: (1) an admission-level SLO Sheath that reduces bursty token admission for tenants approaching short-term SLO budgets, and (2) a Transient Circuit Attenuator that prevents fast flip-flops by introducing a soft attenuated state with jittered cooldown. The description below is a single continuous narrative that contains the motivation, design, commits, changed files summary, review thread, CI summary, and merge details. Motivation: keep applications online while avoiding oscillation and cascading load during short lived regional surges. Design summary: - SLO Sheath: a lightweight token-bucket style soft quota computed per-tenant and per-route using a 60s sliding window and a longer 5m smoothing window for trend detection. When short-window usage would exceed the tenant's short-term SLO allowance, new requests are admitted probabilistically based on remaining budget, with a warm-up factor for recently throttled tenants to avoid hard cutoffs. The controller exposes a conservative admission decision (allow/probabilistic-deny) that integrates with existing request routing so that downstream runtime can still make backlog/hedge decisions. - Transient Circuit Attenuator: extends the circuit state machine with a new 'attenuated' state between CLOSED and OPEN. When error rate or latency crosses the open threshold for a short interval, the circuit moves to ATTENUATED instead of immediate OPEN. In ATTENUATED requests are accepted at a reduced rate (configurable fraction) and are instrumented with lightweight probing. If conditions worsen for a configured hold window, the circuit transitions to OPEN; if conditions improve, it returns to CLOSED. Attenuated transitions use exponential backoff with randomized jitter to prevent synchronized reopens across nodes. Telemetry and safety: added high-cardinality-safe metrics and sparse traces: slo_sheath_admit{tenant,route,decision}, slo_sheath_budget_remaining, circuit_attenuator_state{node,region}, circuit_attenuator_probe_result. We included dashboards and alert rules to surface high-probability attenuated events rather than immediate SLO alerts, with recommended Grafana panels linked in the internal runbook. Configuration and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.feature.slo_sheath and enabled by default for a subset of high-risk regions. We added a rollout plan: stage to canary clusters (10% of region) -> regional ramp -> global. Implementation notes: - admission controller implemented in runtime/slo/slo_sheath.go with a compact decision API so call sites need only a single lines of integration; - circuit changes in runtime/circuit/attenuator.go and runtime/circuit/attenuator_state.go; - config knobs in configs/defaults.yaml and configs/feature-flags.yaml; - telemetry additions in telemetry/metrics.yaml and telemetry/dashboards/slo_sheath.json; - e2e and unit tests under runtime/slo/*_test.go and runtime/circuit/*_test.go; - a small client-side example at redwood-examples/gradual-backoff-demo to demonstrate ATTENUATED behavior. Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: initial slo_sheath admission controller + unit tests - 2b3c4d5: circuit attenuator state machine + probe runner - 3c4d5e6: telemetry + dashboards + runbook pointers - 4d5e6f7: feature flagging + rollout gating + docs - 5e6f7g8: test hardening based on reviewer feedback and flake fixes Changed areas (high-level paths): - runtime/slo/slo_sheath.go - runtime/slo/slo_sheath_test.go - runtime/circuit/attenuator.go - runtime/circuit/attenuator_state.go - runtime/circuit/attenuator_test.go - configs/defaults.yaml - configs/feature-flags.yaml - telemetry/metrics.yaml - telemetry/dashboards/slo_sheath.json - redwood-examples/gradual-backoff-demo/README.md - docs/runbooks/slo_sheath.md Review thread (summary): - Marcus Hale: asked about metric cardinality and suggested aggregating by tenant-cohort instead of raw tenant id; requested an explicit fail-open configuration for private deployments. - Priya (author): replied that metrics use cohort tagging (cohort derived at admission) and added cohort aggregation in telemetry/metrics.yaml; added runtime.config.runtime.sheath.fail_open_for_private to defaults and documented behavior. - Lina Cho: requested deterministic probe scheduling to reduce noise and suggested adding a short probe warmup to avoid flapping on transient network blips. - Priya: implemented probe warmup and switched the probe scheduler to a deterministic seeded jitter window per-node. - Diego Alvarez: asked for unit test showing that ATTENUATED reduces flip rate under synthetic burst; author added load-simulation unit test and an e2e scenario in the examples folder. - Marcus: approved after CI passed and tests stabilized. CI summary: initial CI run had a flaky simulator test; flake fixed in commit 5e6f7g8 and full pipeline green. Checks: unit, integration, linters, telemetry-schema, e2e (canary mode). Merge: squash and merge by Marcus Hale. No database or public API schema changes. Backward compatibility: runtime API for admission decision is additive and optional; existing callers get default ALLOW behavior when feature flag off. Operational impact: operators should monitor slo_sheath_budget_remaining and circuit_attenuator_state for sustained ATTENUATED events. Rollback plan: feature flag off -> immediate revert of admission behavior; circuit returns to prior CLOSED/OPEN only transitions. Post-deploy notes: during canary deployment we observed a 48% reduction in circuit reopen events and a measurable decrease in tail p99 latency during repeat bursts in the canary region. This PR is targeted as a hotfix for short-term incident mitigation and as a stable runtime improvement for long-term oscilliation control.

Marcus Hale: 'Approved — CI green, test coverage acceptable, rollout doc looks solid.'
notes_for_release_engineer: Enable runtime.feature.slo_sheath in canary clusters first. Monitor slo_sheath_budget_remaining and circuit_attenuator_state metrics. If seeing unexpected large-scale denial rates, flip runtime.config.runtime.sheath.fail_open_for_private or disable feature flag.
post_deploy_observations: Canary region saw ~48% fewer circuit reopens during repeated 30s bursts and 12% reduction in tail p99 token latency for affected routes. No significant increase in 5m SLO breach rate observed during the window.
